original_value: Though deep learning has shown successful performance in classifying the label and severity stage of certain disease, most of them give few evidence on how to make prediction. Here, we propose to exploit the interpretability of deep learning application in medical diagnosis. Inspired by Koch’s Postulates, a well-known strategy in medical research to identify the property of pathogen, we define a pathological descriptor that can be extracted from the activated neurons of a diabetic retinopathy detector. To visualize the symptom and feature encoded in this descriptor, we propose a GAN based method to synthesize pathological retinal image given the descriptor and a binary vessel segmentation. Besides, with this descriptor, we can arbitrarily manipulate the position and quantity of lesions. As verified by a panel of 5 licensed ophthalmologists, our synthesized images carry the symptoms that are directly related to diabetic retinopathy diagnosis. The panel survey also shows that our generated images is both qualitatively and quantitatively superior to existing methods.

result.paraphrase: Although deep learning has achieved strong performance in classifying disease labels and severity stages, most methods provide little evidence of how their predictions are made. Here, we aim to leverage the interpretability of deep learning in medical diagnosis. Motivated by Koch’s Postulates, a classic medical research strategy for identifying pathogen properties, we define a pathological descriptor extracted from the activated neurons of a diabetic retinopathy detector. To visualize the symptoms and features encoded in this descriptor, we propose a GAN-based approach to synthesize pathological retinal images from the descriptor and a binary vessel segmentation. In addition, this descriptor lets us arbitrarily control the location and number of lesions. As confirmed by a panel of five licensed ophthalmologists, our synthesized images contain symptoms directly related to diabetic retinopathy diagnosis. The survey also indicates that our generated images are qualitatively and quantitatively superior to existing methods.
